name: Patella
description: Largest sesamoid, between the quadriceps and patellar tendons, with a larger lateral and smaller medial facet divided by a vertical ridge. Axial images show facets, tilt and cartilage; sagittal images show the poles, tendons and patellar height.

normal_values.insall_salvati_ratio: 0.8–1.2 on radiograph; on sagittal MRI alta above 1.3–1.5, baja below 0.74
normal_values.patellotrochlear_index: 12.5–50% on sagittal MRI; below 12.5% alta, above 50% baja

variants_pitfalls: Bipartite patella (about 1–2%, often bilateral) is usually superolateral; smooth corticated margins separate it from a fracture, and edema in the fragment marks a painful one.
Dorsal defect: a round subchondral lesion about 1 cm across in the superolateral patella, with a sclerotic rim and usually intact cartilage; unlike OCD there is no fragment. Mostly incidental.

Transient lateral dislocation: inferomedial patellar osteochondral injury (70%) with lateral femoral condyle edema (80%), often unsuspected clinically. Check the MPFL and medial retinaculum and look for loose bodies.
Wiberg facet shapes I–III are variants, not disease.
